transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-17 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (ClarityHealth CTO), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Engineer), Lena Ortiz (Security Architect)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focusing on final model selection for the pilot, pinning strategy, and an explicit hot-swap / fallback playbook. Customer wants clear rollback windows and a way to hot-swap to a safe, lower-cost model variant if latency or error rates spike. Also covered security checklist (KMS, audit logs), and a plan to run an extended latency/cost sweep on quantized variants.

Topics covered:
- Model catalog comparison: quantized v1/v2, float16 variant, and a smaller latency-optimized model
- Pinning strategy: version vs alias, canary % and freeze windows
- Hot-swap / fallback runbook: triggering metrics and escape hatches
- Security and compliance: KMS, audit logs, data residency concerns
- Next steps: benchmarks, docs, pilot contract updates

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:10] Aisha: hi yep Aisha here.
[00:12] Marco: Marco on the line.
[00:14] Lena: Lena here.
[00:16] Priya: Priya from Redwood. good to see you all.

[00:25] Jordan: cool so agenda is short — finalize model choice for the pilot and pinning approach, and walk through the hot-swap playbook we sketched last week. any additions?
[00:33] Aisha: no that sounds right, but I want to make sure the fallback is non-disruptive; downtime is, uh, highly undesirable for our triage flows.

[00:45] Priya: yeah understood. last week's numbers we posted — the quantized v2 at 8-bit showed about 35% cost savings but adds 25–40ms on tail latency under small batch conditions. if your p50 SLO is tight we can look at streaming and smaller batch sizes to recover some of that.

[01:10] Marco: can you repeat the latency delta? I missed the exact median.
[01:14] Priya: sure it's roughly +35ms p50 and closer to +60ms on p95 in our microbench with 512 token windows, unbatched. with batching the p95 improves but cost advantage reduces.

[01:36] Marco: hmm okay. for our clinical note summarization a lot of requests are short 80–120 tokens so maybe quantized v2 is okay if p95 stays < 450ms.

[01:49] Jordan: good call — so decision fork is, do we pin to quantized v2 as primary with a float16 fallback, or use float16 primary and keep quantized as cost-optimized background?

[02:05] Aisha: priority is correctness and latency, cost is secondary but still material. if the quantized model shows any regression on hallucination or entity wipes we can't accept it.

[02:20] Priya: we recommend a phased pin: start with float16 as primary, run a 2-day shadow of quantized v2 at 20% traffic (we can do traffic mirroring in Redwood Dedicated or the hosted route), measure hallucination/regression with your eval set, then consider switching primary.

[02:42] Marco: the mirroring sounds good. what's the overhead for mirroring? does it double token costs?
[02:48] Priya: mirroring will duplicate requests for the mirrored path so yes it's additional inference cost, but you can mirror only a sample set, not 100%. we suggested a stratified 20% sample focused on high-risk prompts.

[03:05] Lena: from security/compliance side we need audit logs for every model switch plus KMS usage logs for key operations. is that captured?

[03:13] Jordan: yes Redwood audit logs include per-request model id, user id, and option to pipe to your SIEM. KMS integration shows key usage metadata in our control plane; we'll share the SOC 2 + KMS integration doc.

[03:30] Aisha: and data residency? pilot traffic will be US-only, but production might later be EMEA. can we pin region or have regional fallback?

[03:38] Priya: yes, routing policies support region pinning and we can add a region-based fallback so if US capacity is constrained you fail over to an EU-equivalent variant — though that adds latency.

[04:00] Marco: question on pin semantics — do you recommend pinning to a model version id or to an alias that you update? we want traceability for audits.

[04:08] Priya: best practice is to use aliases in your app for day-to-day traffic, and pin the rollout by model version in the deployment policy. the alias points to a version; the control plane keeps history so you get trace logs showing alias changes and the underlying version ids.

[04:30] Jordan: we also discussed a freeze window during business hours: no automated rollouts between 8am–6pm PT, only manual emergency hot-swap. that's in the playbook.

[04:44] Aisha: that's essential. also, we need an explicit escape hatch that switches to a smaller deterministic model that we have validated — basically a safe-mode.

[04:55] Priya: yep we've got a 'safe-mode' pattern: if error-rate > 2% or median latency > 1200ms for 5 consecutive minutes, automatically route 100% to the safe-model alias and notify ops. Safe-model is a smaller float16 variant we validated on your eval set.

[05:20] Marco: what about rollback windows? if we switch to safe-mode, how do we rollback to the prior model without losing state?

[05:28] Priya: two options. short-term hot-swap is stateless: you accept a small divergence in session-level context. long-term rollback requires a freeze period to re-hydrate any KV cache and then can be done with a canary and progressive ramp. we documented both in the runbook.

[05:50] Aisha: okay and who owns the decision to flip to safe-mode — ops or Redwood? we want customer control but also automated safety triggers.

[06:00] Jordan: customer-owned by default, but we can recommend an automated policy that triggers and sends an approval request to ops. if no response in X minutes, it can auto-enforce. we'll make that configurable.

[06:15] Marco: on evaluation — Priya, can you explain the cadence of the hallucination/regression checks? we need thresholds.

[06:20] Priya: yes we run two checks: semantic fidelity (ROUGE-like and entity match) against your red-team set and a human spot check sample. automated thresholds we propose: entity-match >= 98% and semantic score delta < 0.03 vs baseline. anything outside flags for human review.

[06:45] Lena: those thresholds seem reasonable but require auditability of the evaluation runs. can that be exported?

[06:52] Priya: absolutely, all evaluation results are exportable as CSV and tied to a model version id. we'll include the comparison reports in the pilot dashboard.

[07:05] Jordan: quick deep-dive — Marco you sent a request to test KV-cache warmup scenarios?
[07:10] Marco: yes we have a sessioned workflow where context grows across calls and warmup latency impacts early messages. can you simulate long-tail KV warmup?

[07:20] Priya: we can. in Dedicated we can pin workers and reproduce cache cold-starts. we'll run a 48-hour warmup test with representative session patterns and record token-by-token latency.

[07:36] Marco: great, please include an experiment with continuous batching vs micro-batch at 50ms flush. we want to know tradeoffs.

[07:44] Priya: noted. we'll do three variants: pure streaming, micro-batch 50ms, batch with 8 request concurrency. outputs will include cost-per-token estimates.

[08:02] Aisha: on cost — can you clarify how quantized v2 interacts with token pricing? are those discounts baked into pilot pricing?

[08:10] Jordan: pilot pricing will show unit cost by model-id and quantization level. quantized models typically map to a lower unit price in our pricing spreadsheet. I'll send an updated pilot pricing sheet with the three candidate models.

[08:24] Marco: any concerns about safety regressions with quantized v2? we saw a couple of paraphrase cases in the sandbox but not sure if it's noise.

[08:32] Priya: it's model-specific. quantization can change tokenization sensitivity and rare-entity handling; that's why mirroring and the entity-match check are critical. initial sandbox noise isn't definitive.

[08:50] Jordan: ok let's walk the actual hot-swap playbook — Priya, can you read the trigger sequence?

[08:56] Priya: yep: 1) detect — metric breach (error-rate, latency, or hallucination alert) 2) confirm — automated 1-minute re-check to avoid flapping 3) isolate — route 30% traffic to safe-model for a 5 minute canary 4) escalate — notify oncall + create incident ticket 5) enforce — if canary fails, route 100% to safe-model and freeze rollouts 6) postmortem — collect traces and KV cache snapshots.

[09:30] Lena: what telemetry do we capture for the postmortem? we need per-request model id, token counts, KV hits/misses, and client identifiers.

[09:39] Priya: all included. those fields are in the request-level trace. we can stream to your SIEM or S3 retention bucket.

[09:50] Marco: how long are traces kept? retention policy?

[09:53] Jordan: default 30 days, can extend for enterprise. we'll note that in the pilot terms.

[10:05] Aisha: next, access controls — we need role-based access for rollout actions. can we restrict who can trigger a hot-swap?

[10:12] Priya: yes RBAC supports role levels: viewer, operator, deployer, admin. only deployer+ can change alias mappings; operator can trigger safe-mode.

[10:25] Marco: good. also, does the control plane provide a dry-run mode for rollout changes?

[10:29] Priya: yes there's a dry-run that simulates traffic split and logs expected routing without changing production flows.

[10:36] Jordan: let's capture concrete next steps and owners — I'll summarize in the notes and share the runbook + pricing.

[10:45] Aisha: timeline: we want to decide primary model by end of pilot week two. is that feasible?

[10:52] Jordan: yes with the 48h mirroring and 24h warmup tests we can have a recommendation by 2026-06-24.

[11:03] Marco: ok i'll prioritize the red-team prompts and the sample distribution table.

[11:08] Lena: and i'll check with compliance on data residency needs and confirm EMEA requirements.

[11:15] Priya: we'll get the benchmark matrix and the quantized-v2 sweep results back to you by Monday.

[11:25] Jordan: perfect. any final questions?

[11:30] Aisha: one — for emergency manual rollback how long is a typical cache rehydrate? just to set expectations.

[11:36] Priya: depends on session sizes; for your typical 3–5kb sessions it's about 20–90 seconds to warm critical hot keys, full warm for large long-tail could be a few minutes. we will include guidance in the runbook.

[11:50] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll send the pricing and updated runbook and set a follow-up for next Wednesday same time.

[11:58] Marco: thanks.
[12:00] Aisha: thanks all.

End of transcript.
